correctness.rationale: In any rose of t≥2 cycles, the degree-2t center separates in round one. Round-r positions on a length-L petal have identical colors iff their unordered clipped pairs {min(i,r),min(L−i,r)} coincide, hence within a petal last split floor(L/2). Comparing unequal lengths L<M, adjacent-to-center positions agree through round L−1 and split at L; none survive beyond. Over all unequal pairs maximum shorter length is the second-largest distinct petal length λ_{s−1}, independent of multiplicities. If all equal, only the longest-half term matters. Permutations of equal-length petals and reflections give the precise automorphism orbits, identical to stable classes. Independent ordinary WL over 1278 multisets of 2..5 petals, lengths 3..10, agreed with formula.
residual_risks: Simple petals meeting only at center; no other vertex identifications.
This is an all-t theorem via clipped pair induction; finite census only corroborates.

value.rationale: A uniform all-parameter stabilization-depth and orbit theorem for graphs with an arbitrary number of petals is a structural result, not merely a numerical test. The reduction of a multiset of arbitrary cycle lengths to its two dominant distinct scales is mathematically informative and supplies a natural exact benchmark of 1-WL symmetry resolution. The unbounded-petal extension survives beyond the known two-cycle subfamily.
residual_risks: All equal petals and repeated petal lengths are essential boundary cases.

final_claim: For t≥2 cycles C_{L_i} (L_i≥3) meeting at one common vertex, with distinct lengths λ1<...<λs, stabilization depth is floor(λs/2) for s=1, otherwise max(floor(λs/2),λ_{s−1}); stable WL colors equal rose automorphism orbits.
limitations: Simple undirected roses only, t≥2; excludes nonuniform input coloring and general cactus graphs.
Potential prior coverage of orbit statement separate from exact depth novelty.
